o: An alternating subarray lives entirely inside a maximal alternating run. A run of length L contributes L(L+1)/2 subarrays (all its contiguous pieces). Summing over runs gives the answer: [0,1,1,1] has runs of lengths 2 and 1 → 3 + 1 = 5; [1,0,1,0] is one run of 4 → 10.
k: Every alternating subarray belongs to exactly one maximal alternating run.

a.n: Approach 1: Linear scan accumulating run contributions
a.i: Track current run length; whenever alternation breaks, add L(L+1)/2 for the finished run and restart at 1.
s: If nums[i] != nums[i-1], cur++; else add cur*(cur+1)/2 and reset cur = 1.
After the loop add the final run's contribution.

a.i: Alternatively, for each index count the length of the alternating run ending there (`end[i]`); the number of alternating subarrays ending at i equals end[i]. Summing gives the same total without explicit run boundaries.
s: If nums[i] != nums[i-1], end++ else end = 1.
Add end to the answer each step.

w: Answer reaches ~5·10^9 for n = 1e5, so use 64-bit accumulation. Both approaches are equally optimal; Approach 2 is slightly less error-prone (no post-loop flush).
